consent.label: Cookie consent
consent.title: We value your privacy
consent.text: We use cookies and similar tools to run this site, to understand how it is used and to show you relevant ads. Choose what you allow.
consent.necessaryHelp: Needed for the site to work. Always on.
consent.analyticsHelp: Helps us understand how visitors use the site.
consent.marketingHelp: Lets us and our partners show you relevant ads.
notice.label: Announcement
seo.check.robots_txt.title: robots.txt answers
seo.check.robots_txt.not_text: robots.txt answers an HTML page, not plain text, so search engines find no rules in it.
seo.check.robots_txt.missing: robots.txt answered {status}, so search engines read your whole site without rules.
seo.check.robots_txt.error: robots.txt did not answer properly (status {status}; 0 means no answer). While it fails with a server error, Google stops crawling your site.
seo.check.robots_txt.fix: Serve a robots.txt at the root of your site that answers 200 itself. With robots and verification on, your server can answer /robots.txt with what Growth's GET /v1/robots.txt gives (see the docs).
seo.check.robots_sitemap.title: robots.txt names your sitemap
seo.check.robots_sitemap.fix: Add a Sitemap line with your sitemap's full address, for example Sitemap: https://shop.example.com/sitemap.xml (Settings → robots and verification → Sitemaps), so every search engine finds it.
seo.check.robots_blocks.title: robots.txt lets Google read your pages
seo.check.robots_blocks.ok: Google may read the home page, the sitemap, the pages checked and the product images (addresses tried: {count}).
seo.check.robots_blocks.blocked: robots.txt keeps Google from {count} of the addresses checked, for example {path} ({rule}).
seo.check.robots_blocks.fix: Remove or narrow that rule so it does not block pages, product images or the sitemap you want in search results, then ask Search Console to crawl again. Block only what should stay out of search, such as cart, checkout and account pages.
seo.check.sitemap.title: A sitemap is reachable
seo.check.sitemap.ok: The sitemap lists {count} addresses (in the files read).
seo.check.sitemap.missing: The sitemap answered {status} (0 means no answer).
seo.check.sitemap.invalid: The sitemap address does not answer a sitemap (no urlset or sitemapindex).
seo.check.sitemap.too_large: The sitemap is larger than 16 MB, so no pages could be sampled from it. Split it into a sitemap index of smaller files.
seo.check.sitemap.file_missing: A file of the sitemap index answered {status}: {path}.
seo.check.sitemap.fix: Publish a sitemap of your pages (Ecommerce serves one), with at most 50,000 addresses per file, list it in robots.txt with a Sitemap line, then submit it in Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.
seo.check.sitemap_urls.title: Sitemap addresses answer 200
seo.check.sitemap_urls.ok: The sitemap addresses read answered 200 (addresses read: {count}).
seo.check.sitemap_urls.bad: {count} of the sitemap addresses read do not answer 200, for example {path} ({status}).
seo.check.sitemap_urls.other_host: {count} sitemap addresses are not https addresses of this website, for example {url}.
seo.check.sitemap_urls.fix: List only pages that answer 200 themselves (no redirects, missing pages or errors), each with its full https address on this website: the address the page names as its canonical.
seo.check.soft_404.title: Missing pages answer 404
seo.check.soft_404.ok: {path}, an address your site does not have, answered {status}.
seo.check.soft_404.moved: {path}, a removed product's address from your 404 log, now sends visitors permanently ({status}) to another product page, {location}.
seo.check.soft_404.soft: {path}, an address your site does not have, answered 200 (a soft 404), so search engines may index empty pages.
seo.check.soft_404.redirect: {path}, an address your site does not have, redirects ({status}) to {location}; Google treats that as a soft 404.
seo.check.soft_404.error: {path}, an address your site does not have, answered {status} (0 means no answer).
seo.check.soft_404.fix: Answer every address your site does not have with the HTTP status 404 (or 410) and a helpful page, with the not_found marker so Growth logs it; a product page your server renders as not found answers 404 too, never 200. Send a removed product to its replacement and other old addresses to their new page with a permanent redirect, instead of sending every missing page to its category or the home page.
seo.check.redirects_live.title: Redirect rules work on your site
seo.check.redirects_live.ok: The old paths of the redirect rules tried answered as their rules say (rules tried: {count}).
seo.check.redirects_live.not_applied: {count} of the redirect rules tried are not applied, for example {path} answered {status} instead of {expected}.
seo.check.redirects_live.fix: Make your website's server ask Growth before it answers (GET /v1/redirects/match, or the whole list in edge middleware; see the docs) and answer with the rule's code and Location.
seo.check.redirect_suggestions.title: Missing pages have a redirect
seo.check.redirect_suggestions.none: Every address visitors could not find in the last 90 days has a redirect rule.
seo.check.redirect_suggestions.some: {count} addresses visitors could not find in the last 90 days have no redirect rule, most of all {path} ({hits} visits).
seo.check.redirect_suggestions.fix: Open Redirects and add a rule from its suggestions for each address that has a new page (turn on Redirects if it is off).
seo.check.verification.title: Search engine verification
seo.check.verification.ok: The home page carries a verification tag (tags: {count}).
seo.check.verification.none: The home page carries no verification tag.
seo.check.verification.fix: Add your site in Google Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools or Yandex Webmaster, choose the HTML tag method, paste the tag's content into the robots and verification settings and include Growth's verification tags in your page head.
seo.check.web_vitals_site.title: Core Web Vitals of your visitors
seo.check.web_vitals_site.ok: LCP, INP and CLS were good for at least 75% of the visits measured in the last 28 days (measurements: {samples}).
seo.check.web_vitals_site.needs_improvem: {vital} was good for {good}% of the visits measured in the last 28 days; Google wants at least 75%.
seo.check.web_vitals_site.poor: {vital} was good for only {good}% of the visits measured in the last 28 days, and poor for more than a quarter of them.
seo.check.web_vitals_site.fix: See the slowest pages in the analytics dashboard (with the sessions detail) and make them faster: a quick server answer, the main image early and not lazy, images with width and height, and less script work on taps.
seo.check.reachable.title: The page opens
seo.check.reachable.not_found: The page answered {status}: it does not exist.
seo.check.reachable.timeout: The page did not answer within 8 seconds.
seo.check.reachable.too_large: The page is larger than 2 MB; Google reads only the first 2 MB of a page.
seo.check.reachable.unreachable: The page could not be reached: its address does not answer or is not a public https address.
seo.check.reachable.not_read: Not read: the check reached its time limit first. Check this page on its own from its menu.
seo.check.reachable.fix: Make sure the page exists and answers 200 itself, quickly, without sending visitors to another address, and link to its final address everywhere.
seo.check.noindex.title: The page can be indexed
seo.check.noindex.ok: Nothing on the page keeps it out of search results.
seo.check.noindex.noindex: The page says noindex (a robots meta tag or an X-Robots-Tag header).
seo.check.noindex.in_sitemap: Your sitemap lists the page, but it says noindex: the two contradict each other.
seo.check.noindex.fix: Remove noindex if the page should appear in search results; if it should not, leave it out of your sitemap.
seo.check.title.title: Page title
seo.check.title.long: The title has {length} characters; search results cut it after about 60.
seo.check.title.fix: Give every page its own title of about 10 to 60 characters that says what the page is.
seo.check.description.title: Meta description
seo.check.description.missing: The page has no meta description.
seo.check.description.short: The meta description has only {length} characters.
seo.check.description.long: The meta description has {length} characters; search results cut it after about 160.
seo.check.description.fix: Add a meta description of about 50 to 160 characters that sums up the page.
seo.check.h1.title: One main heading
seo.check.h1.ok: The page has one h1 heading.
seo.check.h1.missing: The page has no h1 heading in the HTML your server sends.
seo.check.h1.fix: Use exactly one h1 heading per page, with the page's main topic (for a product, its name), in the HTML your server sends.
seo.check.canonical.title: Canonical address
seo.check.canonical.ok: The page names itself as its canonical address.
seo.check.canonical.missing: The page has no canonical link.
seo.check.canonical.several: The page has {count} different canonical links, so search engines ignore them all.
seo.check.canonical.relative: The canonical link is not a full address: {url}.
seo.check.canonical.other_host: The canonical link points to another site: {url}.
seo.check.canonical.other_page: The canonical link points to another page: {url}. That is right for a copy of that page, but wrong for a page you want in search results.
seo.check.canonical.not_self: Your sitemap lists the page, but its canonical link points to another page: {url}.
seo.check.canonical.invalid: The canonical link is not a valid address: {url}.
seo.check.canonical.fix: Put one canonical link in the page head with the full https address of the page's preferred version on this website (for most pages, its own address), and list only canonical addresses in your sitemap.
seo.check.lang.title: Page language
seo.check.lang.missing: The page's html tag has no lang attribute.
seo.check.lang.fix: Set the page's language on its html tag, for example lang="en".
seo.check.viewport.title: Fits phones
seo.check.viewport.ok: The page has the viewport meta tag.
seo.check.viewport.missing: The page has no viewport meta tag.
seo.check.viewport.fix: Add the viewport meta tag (width=device-width, initial-scale=1) so the page fits phone screens.
seo.check.social.title: Social sharing tags
seo.check.social.ok: The page has og:title and og:image.
seo.check.social.missing: The page misses og:title or og:image.
seo.check.social.fix: Add the og:title and og:image meta tags so shared links show a title and a picture.
seo.check.image_alt.title: Image descriptions
seo.check.image_alt.ok: Every image has an alt text.
seo.check.image_alt.fix: Give every image an alt text that describes it; use an empty alt for decorative images.
seo.check.image_size.title: Image sizes
seo.check.image_size.ok: Every image states its width and height.
seo.check.image_size.missing: {count} images do not state their width and height, so the page moves while they load (layout shift).
seo.check.image_size.fix: Add width and height attributes (the image's own size) to every img tag; CSS can still scale it.
seo.check.structured_data.title: Structured data
seo.check.structured_data.ok: The page's structured data reads (JSON-LD blocks: {count}).
seo.check.structured_data.none: The page has no JSON-LD structured data.
seo.check.structured_data.invalid: {count} JSON-LD blocks are not valid JSON, so search engines ignore them.
seo.check.structured_data.fix: Add JSON-LD structured data in a script of type application/ld+json (Organization and WebSite on the home page, Product and BreadcrumbList where they fit), make sure it is valid JSON, and test the page in Google's Rich Results Test.
seo.check.site_data.title: Business and site name data
seo.check.site_data.ok: The home page describes your business (Organization) and your site (WebSite).
seo.check.site_data.missing: The home page's structured data has no {missing}.
seo.check.site_data.fix: Add Organization (or OnlineStore) structured data with your business name, logo and address of your site, and WebSite with your site's name, to the home page; Google uses them for your logo and site name in search results.
seo.check.product_data.title: Product data for Google
seo.check.product_data.ok: The product's structured data has its name, images and offers with price, currency and availability.
seo.check.product_data.incomplete: The product's structured data lacks {missing}, so it cannot show as a product in Google.
seo.check.product_data.fix: Give the Product (or each variant of a ProductGroup) its name, image and an Offer with price, priceCurrency and availability; Ecommerce's SEO answers carry them all.
seo.check.price_match.title: The page shows the price
seo.check.price_match.ok: The page shows the price of its structured data ({price} {currency}).
seo.check.price_match.not_shown: The HTML your server sends does not show the price of the page's structured data ({price} {currency}); Google checks that they match.
seo.check.price_match.fix: Show the same price in the HTML your server sends as in the structured data (use the same answer for both); a price drawn only by a script, or a different one, can keep the product out of Google.
seo.check.server_html.title: Product content in your server's HTML
seo.check.server_html.ok: The HTML your server sends names the product ({name}).
seo.check.server_html.missing: The HTML your server sends does not name the product ({name}); only a script draws it.
seo.check.server_html.fix: Render the product's name, price and main content into the HTML on your server (Ecommerce's docs show server-side snippets), so search engines read it without running scripts.
seo.check.breadcrumbs.title: Breadcrumbs
seo.check.breadcrumbs.ok: The page's structured data has a BreadcrumbList.
seo.check.breadcrumbs.missing: The page's structured data has no BreadcrumbList.
seo.check.breadcrumbs.fix: Show breadcrumb links on the page (home, category, page) and describe them with BreadcrumbList structured data; Ecommerce's SEO answers carry it.
seo.check.response_time.title: Server response time
seo.check.response_time.slow: The page took {ms} ms to answer; aim for 800 ms or less.
seo.check.response_time.very_slow: The page took {ms} ms to answer; more than 1,800 ms is poor.
seo.check.response_time.fix: Make your server answer faster: cache pages and the answers they are built from, do no slow work before the page is sent, and host it near your visitors. This is measured from our server, so allow for the distance.
seo.check.caching.title: Caching headers
seo.check.caching.ok: The page sends an ETag or Last-Modified header, so search engines can read it again cheaply.
seo.check.caching.none: The page sends neither an ETag nor a Last-Modified header.
seo.check.caching.no_store: The page sends Cache-Control: {cacheControl}, so nothing may keep it: search engines and browsers download it whole every time, even with an ETag.
seo.check.caching.fix: Send an ETag (or Last-Modified) header that changes only when the page's content changes, with a Cache-Control that lets it be kept (for example private, no-cache, or a short max-age; never no-store): Google then asks with If-None-Match, and a 304 answer saves your server work and your crawl.
seo.check.web_vitals.title: Web Vitals of pages like this
seo.check.web_vitals.ok: Pages like {pattern} were good on average over the last 28 days (measurements: {samples}).
seo.check.web_vitals.needs_improvement: Pages like {pattern} need improvement: {vital} averaged {value} over the last 28 days (measurements: {samples}).
seo.check.web_vitals.poor: Pages like {pattern} are poor: {vital} averaged {value} over the last 28 days (measurements: {samples}).
seo.check.web_vitals.fix: Make these pages faster and steadier: a quick server answer, the main image early and not lazy, images with width and height, and less script work on taps.
analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.timeZone: Days are in the {timeZone} time zone.
analytics.empty: Nothing recorded in these days yet.
analytics.liveHelp: Seen in the last 5 minutes, on these pages:
analytics.liveNone: Nobody has been on the site in the last 5 minutes.
analytics.trafficHelp: What visitors look at, where they come from and what they use.
analytics.funnelHelp: From viewing an item to buying it.
analytics.searchesHelp: What visitors look for, and the pages they cannot find.
analytics.vitalsHelp: How fast and steady pages are for real visitors.
analytics.journeysHelp: The latest visits of these days, step by step.
analytics.noJourneys: No visits in these days yet.
analytics.eventsHelp: Every recorded event, newest first; kept {months} months.
analytics.problem.range: Pick a first day on or before the last day, at most 366 days apart.
seo.title: SEO checklist
seo.pages: Checks {count} pages ({pages}) and sample pages from your sitemap
seo.notRun: Not checked yet: press Check my pages.
seo.recent: Checked {time}, less than 5 minutes ago: these are those results.
seo.richResults: Test in Google's Rich Results Test
seo.pagesHelp: Paths on your website, one per line; the home page is always checked, at most 20 pages.
seo.problem.paths: Check at most 20 pages at a time.
seo.problem.rate_limited: The checklist runs at most 10 times an hour. Try again later.
indexnow.title: IndexNow
indexnow.help: New or changed pages of this website, one address per line. Search engines that take IndexNow (Bing, Yandex and others) hear about them at once.
indexnow.keyAt: Your site must serve your key at {url}.
indexnow.noKey: Set your IndexNow key in Settings first.
indexnow.badPath: The key file address in Settings is not a path on your website.
indexnow.problem.urls: Send 1 to 10,000 addresses, each an https address of this website.
indexnow.problem.rate_limited: At most 10 submissions an hour. Try again later.
indexnow.refused.key: IndexNow did not accept the key. Your site must serve it at the key file address.
indexnow.refused.host: IndexNow says the addresses do not match the key's website.
indexnow.refused.busy: IndexNow asks for fewer submissions. Try again later.
indexnow.refused.other: IndexNow did not take them. Try again later.
redirects.title: Redirects
redirects.sub: {count} of 5,000 rules: old addresses of your website and the page each goes to.
redirects.match.prefix: This path and every path under it
redirects.none: No rules yet. Add one, import a CSV file or start from a suggestion below.
redirects.help: Visitors and search engines that ask for the old path go to the new page; a 410 rule tells them the page is gone for good. The rest of a path and its query string go along.
redirects.deleteHelp: Visitors who ask for {from} then get your website's own answer, usually its 404 page.
redirects.import.title: Import rules from a CSV file
redirects.import.help: One rule per line with the columns from, match, to, code and note (an export from here, or a file with Redirect from and Redirect to columns). A rule whose old path already has one is changed; nothing is deleted. Check the file first: nothing changes until you import it.
redirects.import.summary: {rows} lines: {created} new, {updated} changed, {unchanged} already as written.
redirects.import.checked: Checked: see what would change below.
redirects.import.problems: Problems ({count}): fix them in the file and check again.
redirects.import.stale: The rules changed since the check. Check the file again.
redirects.row.from.required: Line {line}: the old path (from) is empty.
redirects.row.from.not_path: Line {line}: the old path must start with / or be an address on this website.
redirects.row.from.other_host: Line {line}: the old path is an address on another site.
redirects.row.from.query: Line {line}: the old path has ? or #, but rules match the path only.
redirects.row.from.too_long: Line {line}: the old path is longer than 1,000 characters.
redirects.row.from.twice: Line {line}: this old path is already on an earlier line.
redirects.row.match.not_match: Line {line}: match must be exact or prefix.
redirects.row.to.required: Line {line}: the new page (to) is empty; only a 410 rule has none.
redirects.row.to.not_target: Line {line}: the new page must be a path on this website or an https address.
redirects.row.to.not_https: Line {line}: the new page must use https.
redirects.row.to.too_long: Line {line}: the new page is longer than 2,048 characters.
redirects.row.to.gone: Line {line}: a 410 rule has no new page.
redirects.row.to.loop: Line {line}: this makes a redirect loop: {steps}.
redirects.row.to.chain: Line {line}: visitors would pass two redirects: {steps}.
redirects.row.to.removed: Line {line}: this sends visitors to a page another rule removes: {steps}.
redirects.row.note.too_long: Line {line}: the note is longer than 200 characters.
redirects.row.file.unterminated_quote: A quoted field never ends: check the quotes in the file.
redirects.row.file.too_many_rows: The file has more than 5,000 rules.
redirects.row.file.columns: The first line names no from column.
redirects.row.file.too_many: The website would have more than 5,000 rules.
redirects.row.other: Line {line}: this line is not a valid rule.
redirects.suggestions.title: From your 404 log
redirects.suggestions.sub: The pages visitors could not find most in the last {days} days that have no rule yet. Pick one to add its rule.
redirects.suggestions.none: No missing pages without a rule.
redirects.suggestions.off: Searches and 404s is off, so new 404s are not recorded. Turn it on to see the pages visitors cannot find.
redirects.problem.from: Enter the old path, starting with / (for example /old-page), without ? or #.
redirects.problem.to: Enter the new page: a path on your website or an https address.
redirects.problem.csv: Choose a CSV file or paste its text.
redirects.problem.taken: Another rule already redirects {from}: change that rule instead.
redirects.problem.loop: This would make a redirect loop: {steps}.
redirects.problem.chain: This would make visitors pass two redirects: {steps}. Point the first rule straight at the final page.
redirects.problem.gone: This would send visitors to a page another rule removes: {steps}.
redirects.problem.full: A website may have at most 5,000 rules. Delete some first.
redirects.problem.notFound: This rule no longer exists: it was deleted meanwhile.
problem.forbidden: You do not have the permission for this.
problem.feature_off: This feature is switched off for this website.
problem.database_not_connected: Connect the website's database first (Growth dashboard → Connections).
problem.product_unavailable: Growth is not available for this website right now.
problem.rate_limited: Too many requests at once. Try again in a minute.
